requirements.evidence: Migration has every required column, cascade/nullOnDelete FKs and unique (entity_id,email) (create_entity_invites_table.php:15-25). The model normalizes e-mail with an Attribute setter (EntityInvite.php:39-42). It also has a pending scope, VALID_DAYS=7 and the expired() factory state. sendInvite validates, rejects existing members and pending invites, replaces expired/accepted invites, catches UniqueConstraintViolationException, rate-limits only successful invites (RateLimiter::hit after create), queues the mail, writes an audit log and resets the form (Members.php:55-136). PendingInvites accept is idempotent: an atomic claim is followed by firstOrCreate, then session + redirect. An expired invite gives an error on 'invite' (PendingInvites.php:24-71). Onboarding renders the component inside the box after the form, and the <hr> appears only when invites exist (pending-invites.blade.php:4-7). The modal header is ui.members_details; the role select has no empty option; the confirmation modal replaces wire:confirm; removeMember resets state. The mail renders the required strings, and the pt_BR translations are added. Small deviations: decline() on an accepted invite is a silent no-op, and the members view uses ui.name/ui.email keys that the diff does not add.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes (create invite, accept invite/create membership, change role, remove member) are done inline in Livewire components instead of app/Actions/* classes (Members.php:93-106, PendingInvites.php:41-56). Validation uses inline $this->validate([...]) arrays instead of #[Validate] attributes; the diff even removes the existing `use Livewire\Attributes\Validate`. Invite authorization is a hand-rolled abort_unless e-mail check (PendingInvites.php:110), not a policy. The layout runs an Eloquent query with an FQCN inside Blade (default-page.blade.php:69). On the positive side: #[Fillable] is used, the migration has down(), CHANGELOG, business-rules, database-schema and logging docs are updated, and the audit log channel is used per docs.

security.evidence: Every Members action authorizes 'update' on the entity and resolves IDs inside $this->entity (cancelInvite, openMember, selectedMembership() at Members.php:236-243, removeMember). mount now requires 'update', so employees get 403 on the component and the route. PendingInvites resolves the invite and enforces an e-mail match before acting. The separated flag is #[Locked]. Accept uses an atomic claim, and firstOrCreate prevents a role change for an existing member. Output uses {{ }} everywhere, and the mail escapes the entity name (tested). Remaining gap: authorization is the e-mail string match only. The diff does not show that a verified e-mail is required, so someone who registers an unverified account with the invited address could accept the invite.

tests.evidence: Tests cover the whole feature: the model/factory/schema, the mail in both locales including escaping, accept/decline happy paths, forbidden calls by a stranger, unknown id, expired invite, idempotency, no duplicate membership, a locked-property tamper test, onboarding placement with <hr> ordering, and the switcher (InvitesTest.php). MembersTest covers 403 for employees on the component and the route, the foreign-membership tamper for openMember/saveRole/removeMember/cancelInvite, the owner role and invalid roles, last-manager demotion/removal, the confirmation modal, the race condition, the rate limit and quota non-consumption. Weak spots: unauthorized-call tests reach the actions only through the mount 403, and 'confirming removal is forbidden for employees' only asserts the mount 403, so its name overstates what it checks.

simplicity.evidence: Shared logic is extracted (managerCount(), selectedMembership()), and existing policies are reused. E-mail normalization is repeated in three places: trim() in sendInvite, the model setter and mb_strtolower in the forEmail scope plus inviteeInvite. ASSIGNABLE_ROLES now holds a rule string ('in:admin,employee'), concatenated into validation rules.

readability.evidence: Method names are clear, comments are short and explain the why ('Atomic claim: only one concurrent accept proceeds.'), and the style matches the sibling files. sendInvite is long (~80 lines) with several early returns. The ASSIGNABLE_ROLES name no longer matches its value (a validation-rule fragment). The inline \App\Models\UserRole and \App\Models\EntityInvite FQCNs in Blade hurt readability.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. Small additions beyond the spec: Dashboard isManager now uses can('update') and the duplicated members button for non-owners is removed (dashboard.blade.php). The navbar shows the switcher link when pending invites exist (default-page.blade.php:69). The switcher also renders the <hr>. All of these are related and reasonable, but none was requested.

issues.explanation: Invite creation, invite acceptance (membership creation) and role changes are domain writes done inline in Livewire components instead of in app/Actions/* use-case classes as the conventions require.
Validation uses inline $this->validate([...]) arrays instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern on the public properties inviteEmail, inviteRole and memberRole.

The only authorization for accept/decline is a plain e-mail string match, not a policy, and the diff does not show a requirement for a verified e-mail, so an unverified account registered with the invited address could accept the invite.
The layout runs a database query with a fully-qualified model class inside Blade, which puts query logic in the view.
The view uses ui.name and ui.email translation keys that this diff does not add; if they don't already exist, the raw keys will show as table headers.
decline() silently keeps an accepted invite, while the spec says decline deletes the invite; this is defensible but undocumented in the task.

issues.location: tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTest.php ('confirming removal is forbidden for employees')
issues.explanation: The test name claims to check confirmRemoval authorization, but it only asserts that mount returns 403.
ASSIGNABLE_ROLES now holds a validation-rule fragment ('in:admin,employee') rather than a list of roles, so the name is misleading.
Changes to dashboard isManager semantics and the navbar switcher visibility are related but were not requested.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member adds with an invite flow: a normalized entity_invites model and migration, a queued localized mailable, a rate-limited and race-safe sendInvite, an idempotent atomic accept in PendingInvites, a manager-only members page with a detail modal and a removal confirmation modal, and a broad test suite plus updated docs. Functionally it meets essentially every requirement and is well secured and well tested. It deviates from the project conventions: no app/Actions classes for domain writes, inline validation instead of #[Validate], a hand-rolled invitee check instead of a policy, and a query in the layout. So I would approve it with requested follow-ups rather than as is.
